subject: English
title: CISCE curriculum: English, Class VI

source.read: A third-party copy of the Class VI pages of the CISCE curriculum (English: printed pages 1 to 15), hosted by BYJU'S
source.note: UNOFFICIAL SOURCE. The pages do not name their publisher or year, and were read through a text summary of the PDF, not the PDF itself. The official document on cisce.org could not be reached from the build environment. CISCE is understood not to prescribe a textbook for this class, so a school's own book and term plan may order or extend these topics.

licence: Strand names as printed (facts). Every outcome is written by OpenPath in its own words with a pointer to its strand and line; no curriculum text is reproduced.
review: OpenPath curriculum inventory (research from a secondary source; not an educator review)

outcomes.text: Answers questions on a passage heard or read.
outcomes.note: Listen and answer for passages heard; the Reading course for passages read.

outcomes.text: Follows the issues in spoken texts and asks for things to be made clear.
outcomes.note: Listen and answer checks that a spoken passage is followed; asking for things to be made clear is not practised.

outcomes.text: Leads or guides a group discussion with searching questions.
outcomes.note: Speaking is not practised in the app.

outcomes.text: Uses class-level vocabulary to put a point of view.
outcomes.note: Speaking is not practised in the app.

outcomes.text: Gives presentations with comment that names sources or viewpoints.
outcomes.note: Speaking is not practised in the app.

outcomes.text: Stays confident and calm when presenting or questioning opinions.
outcomes.note: Speaking is not practised in the app.

outcomes.text: Answers opposing views logically, with suitable language and gestures.
outcomes.note: Speaking is not practised in the app.

outcomes.text: Analyses the language of newspapers, television, hoardings and advertisements.
outcomes.note: No media texts in the app.

outcomes.text: Changes the way of speaking to suit the setting and the task.
outcomes.note: Speaking is not practised in the app.

outcomes.text: Fits language to its purpose: to persuade, inform or give an opinion.
outcomes.note: Speaking is not practised in the app.

outcomes.text: Adds multimedia and pictures to presentations.
outcomes.note: Outside the app.

outcomes.text: Makes sense of information in different media and explains why it matters.
outcomes.note: No media texts in the app.

outcomes.text: Understands texts, draws conclusions and reads between the lines.
outcomes.note: Reading covers cause and effect and how characters feel; wider inference is not a separate skill yet.

outcomes.text: Grasps the central idea and how the details carry it.
outcomes.note: Reading course: the main idea and details.

outcomes.text: Uses the shape of stories and poems to predict what comes next.
outcomes.note: Reading covers the order of events in stories; there are no poems and no prediction questions.

outcomes.text: Separates the main points from personal opinions or judgements.
outcomes.note: Reading course: fact and opinion.

outcomes.text: Works out what words and phrases mean, including figurative and suggested meanings.
outcomes.note: New words teaches meanings in sentences; figurative meaning is not taught.

outcomes.text: Reads graded literature: stories, plays, poems, travel writing, life stories, reports, speeches and articles.
outcomes.note: The app holds no literature. A school's chosen book can be added through My Books.

outcomes.text: Writes about real or imagined experiences with describing detail and order.
outcomes.note: Writing of this kind is being built separately.

outcomes.text: Writes arguments backed by clear reasons and evidence.
outcomes.note: Writing of this kind is being built separately.

outcomes.text: Writes clearly for the task, the purpose and the reader.
outcomes.note: Writing of this kind is being built separately.

outcomes.text: Gathers and brings together information from print and digital sources.
outcomes.note: Outside the app.

outcomes.text: Uses exact words, a fitting tone and voice, and varied sentences.
outcomes.note: Writing of this kind is being built separately.

outcomes.text: Follows the steps of writing: plan, revise, edit, rewrite.
outcomes.note: Writing of this kind is being built separately.

outcomes.text: Writes at least three paragraphs, about 200 words, on a topic.
outcomes.note: Writing of this kind is being built separately.

outcomes.text: Writes full narratives with actions, thoughts and feelings.
outcomes.note: Writing of this kind is being built separately.

outcomes.text: Arranges sentences in a sensible order.
outcomes.note: Reading covers the order of events; arranging whole sentences into a paragraph is not practised.

outcomes.text: Uses linking words such as firstly, then, later and finally correctly.
Draws on personal experience or real situations.
outcomes.note: Writing of this kind is being built separately.

outcomes.text: Uses words suited to the class for feelings and actions.
outcomes.note: New words teaches level-appropriate words; it is not organised by feelings and actions.

outcomes.text: Writes simple notices, messages and letters.
outcomes.note: Writing of this kind is being built separately.

outcomes.text: Applies the basic rules of grammar and usage in speaking and writing.
outcomes.note: Grammar in use, at the learner's level.

outcomes.text: Uses pronouns in the right form, and reflexive pronouns correctly.
Notices wrong changes in a pronoun's number or person.
Varies sentence patterns for meaning and style.
outcomes.note: Building compound sentences and who or that clauses is practised; choosing a pattern for style is not.

outcomes.text: Uses the words around a word or phrase to work out its meaning.
outcomes.note: New words shows each word in a sentence; working a meaning out from context alone is not practised.

outcomes.text: Uses common prefixes, suffixes and roots as clues to meaning.
outcomes.note: Word parts are not taught yet.

outcomes.text: Uses print and digital references for how a word is said, what it means and its part of speech.
outcomes.note: Outside the app.

outcomes.text: Understands figures of speech where they are used.
outcomes.note: Figures of speech are not taught yet.

outcomes.text: Makes subject and verb agree when a phrase or clause comes between them.
Tells transitive verbs from intransitive ones.
outcomes.note: Naming kinds of verb is not practised; Grammar in use fixes and builds sentences.

outcomes.text: Makes pronouns agree with the nouns they stand for, including words like each and everyone.
outcomes.note: Matching a pronoun to its noun is practised; words like each and everyone are not yet.

outcomes.text: Keeps verb tenses steady across paragraphs.
outcomes.note: Practised within a sentence, not across a paragraph.

outcomes.text: Spells frequently used words correctly.
outcomes.note: The Spelling Bee, and words misspelt in writing that return as My tricky words.

outcomes.text: Forms and uses the perfect tenses.
Notices wrong changes of tense.
